49c7fb85-122a-4623-9516-858381567fd5.description: Error ratio over 5m is above 14.4x the 1% error budget (fast burn); at this rate a 30-day budget lasts about 2 days.

facts.statement: checkout revision 2 was created at 19:32:03Z with change-cause 'payment client moved to port 9999'. The alert opened at 19:34:33Z.
The only pod-template difference between checkout revisions 1 and 2 is PAYMENT_ADDR, changed from payment:8080 to payment:9999.
The payment Deployment has one revision (18:45:56Z) and no events after startup. Its only logged lines end at 19:32:03Z, and it shows no error-level logs.
In the failing checkout traces, the PaymentService/Charge client span fails with 'dial tcp 10.96.197.163:9999: i/o timeout'. PlaceOrder fails with Unavailable, and frontend returns HTTP 500.
All 18 feature flags are off, so no flag change explains the incident.
No checkout or payment pod restarts, OOM kills, or failed probes appear in the event window. The new checkout pod started cleanly at 19:32:03-05Z.
Checkout's 5m error ratio was 0 from about 19:15 to 19:30 and rose to 0.53-0.56 at 19:37-19:39.5Z.
Only checkout PlaceOrder and payment Charge show server or client error series. Other dependencies show no errors.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Apply the rollback, then watch service:sli_error_ratio:rate5m for checkout and checkout client Charge errors, and confirm payment spans reappear.
hypotheses.statement: Reverting PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:8080 (or rolling back to revision 1) will drop checkout's PaymentService/Charge ERROR rate and the 5m error ratio to near 0 within minutes.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the payment Service ports and endpoints, and any NetworkPolicy in otel-demo, and run a connection test from a checkout pod to payment:9999 and payment:8080.
hypotheses.statement: The payment Service may not expose port 9999, or a network policy may drop that path, which would explain i/o timeouts instead of connection refused.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Query payment pod logs and events for 19:00-19:20Z, and the flagd state history over that window.
hypotheses.statement: The earlier 19:05-19:10 payment Charge error burst may be a separate intermittent payment-side fault, possibly tied to a flag or a restart not captured in the data.

inferences.statement: Checkout's config points at a port payment does not serve, so checkout's charges fail after the 19:32 rollout. This explains the error onset and the timeout signature.
Payment's silence after 19:32Z is most likely because no traffic reaches it, not because payment failed. Its own side shows no errors and no changes, so payment is a symptom, not the root cause.

root_causes.cause: Bad config in rollout revision 2 (19:32:03Z): PAYMENT_ADDR changed from payment:8080 to payment:9999. The port is wrong, so every payment Charge dial times out and about 47% of checkout requests fail.
Earlier intermittent Charge errors (peak about 0.105 near 19:10Z, cleared by 19:20Z) with no explanation yet. This is separate from the current incident and not the current cause.

diagnosis.summary: ErrorBudgetBurn on checkout started with checkout revision 2 (19:32:03Z), whose only change is PAYMENT_ADDR moved from payment:8080 to payment:9999. Checkout's failing PaymentService/Charge calls time out dialing payment:9999, and payment, unchanged since 18:45Z with no own-side errors, has no traffic after 19:32Z. The fix is most likely to restore PAYMENT_ADDR to payment:8080 (or roll back to revision 1) and confirm that the error ratio drops. The earlier 19:05-19:10 payment-side Charge error burst is not explained by this change and remains open.
